text: When core code is changed, keep imports within core: src/core imports only its own files, including nested files and every module form. Core stays independent of replaceable adapters; scripts/boundaries.ts holds the layer map and fails on a forbidden import.
When the CLI receives an unknown command it fails with exit 64 and a message naming the command, and never forwards it to another binary.

A change is integrated only after the full aggregate Check from GitHub Actions passes on the exact HEAD; lint, typecheck and touched tests run locally with npm run fast, then the PR auto-merges on the Check.

Agent state written for this repository stays under .krn/: notes, plans, logs and scratch files go to ignored .krn/runs/<owner>/ or .krn/tmp/ paths, never to tracked project files or the repository root.
Task status lives in tasks/<id>.json and only the lead changes it with krn task (ready, claim, release, close). A worker never edits, closes or deletes a tracker file, even when its task is finished.
A worker receives the task id in its brief and uses it in every commit title, ending the title with the id in parentheses, for example `Add a parser (<task id>)`.
Commits for a managed task carry a `Ticket: <id>` trailer when the change completes the task, or a `Refs: <id>` trailer when it is one step and leaves the task open; no other trailer is required.
Every integration or forward is tested against its real receiver or a verbatim capture of its output.
The lead keeps context bounded: delegate reading to a subagent returning a verdict and path, pass pointers instead of file contents, and verify with commands that print a verdict.
When a defect is fixed, its regression test goes at the lowest layer that reproduces it.
Name files, functions, tests and work by purpose and role, never by phase, slice, ticket, round, date or version: no task ids or dates in new file names or identifiers.
Use Conventional Commits for authored commits, PR titles and squash subjects.

Code and JSON must pass Biome: before every commit run npm run fast (biome --write, tsc, related tests), not only your own tests; generated files such as scripts/lib/shard-weights.mjs must pass Biome too.
KRN-created state uses ignored .krn/worktrees/<branch>/, .krn/runs/<owner>/, .krn/sources/, .krn/tmp/ or .krn/task-claims/ paths; host tool configuration is exempt.
Prefer deep modules with small interfaces and substantial work behind them.
Use one writer per outcome at a time; parallel implementation uses isolated worktrees and returns through one integration.
Never pipe a check run into a filter: redirect it to a log, read the exit code, then read the log.
A new test file needs a weight in scripts/lib/shard-weights.mjs; npm run fast reports a missing one.
Tests use node:test and node:assert/strict under test/, mirroring the src area they cover.
